Who is Rene Haas? Arm CEO emerges as potential Nvidia chief after Jensen Huang’s exit; what makes him a frontrunner?
sum: Nvidia has reportedly approached Arm Holdings chief executive Rene Haas as it explores potential successors to Jensen Huang, according to a Financial Times report.
Haas, who spent seven years at Nvidia before joining Arm in 2013, is among several names being reportedly considered for the top job at the US chipmaker.
However, there is no certainty that Haas will be offered the position or agree to take it up.
Rene Haas is an American technology executive who has led Arm Holdings since February 2022. He has more than three decades of experience in the semiconductor and computing industries.

Haas spent seven years at Nvidia, rising to vice president and general manager of its computing products business. His familiarity with Nvidia and experience leading Arm make him a reported contender.
Under Haas, Arm expanded its focus into areas including AI, data centres, automotive computing and high-performance processors. He also oversaw Arm’s Nasdaq IPO in September 2023.
No. Reports have named Haas as a possible successor, but Nvidia has not confirmed him for the role. There is no certainty he will be offered the position or accept it.

Reliance stock linked to preliminary $1 billion Mahanadi gas hub
sum: Reliance Industries is part of a preliminary proposal to develop shared offshore infrastructure with ONGC and BP in India's Mahanadi basin. The concept could lower development costs for smaller deepwater discoveries, but it has not reached an investment decision.

Maritime Gateway reported on Tuesday, November 10, that Reliance, ONGC and BP were examining a shared facility for producing and evacuating natural gas and condensate from deepwater and ultra-deepwater discoveries off India's east coast. The report attributed the discussions to two industry executives and said the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas was understood to have proposed the initiative.

The proposed model would allow several operators to pool production and evacuation infrastructure rather than build separate systems for individual discoveries. That could improve the commercial prospects of smaller or marginal fields by spreading capital spending across multiple users.

The facility's design is still open. A floating production, storage and offloading unit and a fixed offshore installation are both under consideration. The reported development period is at least three to four years, not a confirmed commissioning schedule. Other producers could potentially use the infrastructure for a fee.

Technical consultants are expected to assess the proposal, while the companies and ministry have not publicly confirmed the investment. The financial effect for Reliance therefore depends on technical findings, commercial arrangements, regulatory steps and any final investment decision.

For investors, the proposal points to a possible way to reduce duplicated offshore infrastructure and support future gas monetisation. It does not yet establish project ownership, financing, capacity or a construction timetable.

sum: Jefferies Stock Picks: A potential revival in foreign portfolio investor (FPI) flows could put largecap stocks in the spotlight, with companies such as Reliance IndustriesKotak Mahindra Bank

In a latest report, global brokerage house Jefferies said that it believes largecaps are better placed to attract foreign money because of their higher liquidity and greater FPI ownership, following a prolonged period of overseas investor selling.

The brokerage has identified 12 stocks that could benefit from a reversal in foreign flows: Reliance Industries, HDFC Bank, Axis Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank, Max Healthcare, JSW Energy, UltraTech CementIndian Hotels Company

"Given higher liquidity and FPI ownership, we see large caps as the more direct beneficiary of revival in FPI flows. We highlight Reliance, HDFC Bank, Axis, Kotak, Max Health, JSW Energy, Ultratech, Indigo, Varun, IHCL, DLF, Sona BLW as plays on FPI reversal," said Jefferies analysts Abhinav Sinha, Priyank Shah and Aditi Singla.

FPI flows into Indian equities have shown signs of turning around after a sustained period of outflows. Foreign investors have recorded net inflows of $8.2 billion since mid-October, including $5.8 billion in just six trading sessions in November 2026.

This marks a potential shift after FPIs recorded cumulative net outflows of $61 billion since September 2024. The first 10 months of 2026 alone saw foreign investors withdraw $31 billion from Indian equities, according to Jefferies.

The brokerage identified several factors that could support a sustained recovery. These include a possible reversal or broadening of the concentrated artificial intelligence (AI) trade, potential equity tax relief, resilient domestic economic conditions, relatively reasonable largecap valuations and light foreign investor positioning in India.

sum: The BSE and NSE will carry a special session on Sunday due to the auspicious trading muhurat of Diwali. This will be a one-hour special session on November 8, 2026, having all block deal sessions, pre-open sessions, and normal market sessions. In the past two Muhurat sessions, both Sensex and NIfty have gained significantly. The 2026 muhurat trading session will mark the beginning of Samvat 2083 on the Indian stock market.

Today, the session begins with block deals from 1:50 PM to 2:05 PM. Right after this, a pre-opening session will be commenced on BSE and NSE from 2:05 pm to 2:20 pm. This will be followed by the normal muhurat trading session of 2:20 pm to 3:30 pm, where investors can buy and sell. The closing auction timing is from 3:20 pm to 3:35 pm for eligible securities. The post-closing session will be from 3:50 PM to 4:00 PM.

All trade that takes place on November 8, 2026, will have its settlement carried out on November 9, 2026. The trading session will follow the T+1 settlement cycle, with settlement scheduled for 9 November.
For smooth clearance of your buying and selling during muhurat trading, investors should ensure they have have sufficient shares and funds in their demat account.
- Muhurat Trading is a regular, live exchange trading session and is neither drill nor a paper-trading session.
- All applicable brokerage, STT, GST, exchange charges and stamp duty will apply on trades in Muhurat trading.
- Normal margin and risk-management requirements will also be in place.

sum: New Delhi, Nov. 3 -- Reliance Industries share price: Reliance Industries share price declined over 1% in intraday trade on Tuesday, November 3, on profit booking after rallying nearly 12% in the previous session. The stock fell as much as 1.3% to an intraday low of Rs.1,281.55 on the NSE, giving back some of Monday's sharp gains.

Reliance Industries shares had surged 11.6% on Monday to close at Rs.1,300, their highest level since early September. The rally marked the stock's biggest single-day gain since April 2020 and helped lift the Nifty 50 by 1.7%, given the company's heavyweight presence in the index.

The sharp rebound also added Rs.1.84 lakh crore to Reliance Industries' market capitalisation, taking it to Rs.17.6 lakh crore and helping it retain its position as India's most valuable listed company. At its peak of Rs.1,611, the company had commanded a market capitalisation of Rs.21.8 lakh crore. It had crossed the Rs.21 lakh crore milestone in June 2024, becoming the first Indian company to achieve the feat.

Despite Monday's rally, Reliance shares remain down 17.22% so far in 2026. The stock had been under pressure for much of the year, closing lower in eight of the previous 10 months. The latest gains followed the company's record quarterly profit, which renewed investor interest in the stock.

Reliance Industries reported a record consolidated profit after tax (PAT) of Rs.29,550 crore for Q2FY27, marking a 33.8% increase from Rs.22,092 crore in the year-ago quarter. Revenue rose 27.8% year-on-year (YoY) to Rs.3,62,268 crore, while EBITDA increased 23.9% to a record Rs.62,409 crore.

The oil-to-chemicals (O2C) business was the biggest contributor to the strong performance. Its EBITDA surged 67.9% to Rs.25,203 crore, supported by higher global fuel margins and improved petrochemical spreads. O2C revenue increased 44.2% to Rs.2,31,601 crore, with supply disruptions in West Asia and other regions pushing transportation fuel cracks higher.

Digital services also supported earnings, while retail remained a relative weak spot. Reliance Retail Ventures reported a 24.3% decline in PAT to Rs.2,611 crore, despite a 6.4% rise in revenue to Rs.91,716 crore. Its EBITDA, before a one-time impairment charge, fell 8.6% to Rs.6,228 crore.

RIL stock opened at Rs.1,228.10 apiece on NSE today, as compared to previous close of Rs.1,164.90 last week on Friday and touched an intraday high of Rs.1,237.30 on 2 November.

Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL) reported a 33.8% year-on-year (YoY) growth in consolidated profit after tax (PAT), including its share of associates and joint ventures, at Rs.29,550 crore for Q2FY27, compared with Rs.22,092 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Net profit attributable to the company's shareholders increased 40% YoY to Rs.25,548 crore.

The company's consolidated revenue rose 27.8% YoY to Rs.3,62,268 crore, while EBITDA increased 23.9% to a record Rs.62,409 crore. The latest quarterly profit also surpassed the Rs.23,196 crore recorded in the previous quarter, marking a fresh high for India's largest listed company by market capitalisation.

The oil-to-chemicals (O2C) segment was the biggest contributor to earnings growth, supported by stronger global transportation fuel cracks and an improvement in petrochemical margins. The segment's EBITDA surged 67.9% YoY to Rs.25,203 crore, while revenue climbed 44.2% to Rs.2,31,601 crore.

Global supply disruptions arising from the West Asia conflict, including tensions surrounding the Strait of Hormuz, as well as attacks on refining infrastructure across the region and Russia, drove fuel cracks to 3-3.7 times their year-ago levels. Meanwhile, the average price of Dated Brent crude stood at $97 per barrel during the quarter, registering a 40.6% YoY increase.

The improvement in refining margins came despite geopolitical uncertainties, higher crude premiums and elevated freight costs. Reliance said its diversified crude procurement strategy and flexibility in optimising product placement helped it capitalise on favourable market conditions. The company also achieved its highest-ever crude processing volumes by increasing supplies from the Americas and the Mediterranean and redirecting exports towards markets offering better net realisations.

The O2C business emerged as the biggest contributor to earnings growth, benefiting from stronger global transportation fuel cracks and improving petrochemical margins. EBITDA from the segment jumped 67.9% year-on-year to Rs.25,203 crore, while revenue rose 44.2% to Rs.2,31,601 crore.

sum: NEW DELHI: Jio Platforms Limited, Reliance Industries’ digital and telecom arm, made a strong stock market debut on Wednesday, October 28, with its shares opening at a 21.36 per cent premium to the IPO issue price. The listing propelled the company to a market valuation of approximately Rs 12.5 lakh crore, making it India’s second-most valuable listed company after its parent, Reliance Industries.

The shares opened at Rs 1,358 apiece on both the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) and National Stock Exchange (NSE), against the issue price of Rs 1,119. The strong debut followed India’s largest initial public offering, valued at approximately Rs 30,213 crore, which witnessed overwhelming demand from institutional and retail investors.

The stock subsequently extended its gains and closed its first trading session at Rs 1,419, approximately 26.81 per cent above the IPO price. The Jio Platforms IPO marked a major return to the primary market for the Reliance Group, approximately two decades after Reliance Petroleum’s public offering in 2006.

The listing marks a significant milestone for the Reliance Group, strengthening its dominance in India’s corporate landscape and highlighting investor confidence in the country’s rapidly expanding digital economy. It also represented another milestone in the group’s expansion beyond its traditional energy and petrochemicals businesses.
The issue attracted more than one crore investor applications, reflecting widespread participation. The supplied report puts the figure at 1.34 crore, although published estimates vary.
Jio Platforms raised approximately Rs 30,213 crore through its public offering, surpassing Hyundai Motor India’s Rs 27,870-crore IPO and LIC’s Rs 21,008-crore issue.
The offering became a landmark event in India’s primary equity market.

sum: Jio Platforms, the digital and telecom business of Reliance Industries, has made a historic stock market debut on October 28, 2026, with its shares opening at a 21.36 percent premium following India’s largest initial public offering (IPO) of ₹30,213 crore.

Jio Platforms shares opened at ₹1,358 on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) and Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), compared with the IPO issue price of ₹1,119. The ₹239 increase per share reflected strong investor demand for India’s largest telecom operator and its expanding digital services business.

The listing valued Jio Platforms at approximately ₹12.5 lakh crore, making it India’s second-most valuable listed company after Reliance Industries. Jio also overtook Bharti Airtel and HDFC Bank in market capitalization.
The IPO marked Reliance Industries’ first major stock market listing in two decades and delivered the strongest debut premium among India’s five largest IPOs by issue size.
Jio Platforms’ ₹30,213 crore IPO attracted bids worth more than ₹7.4 lakh crore, demonstrating substantial investor interest in India’s telecommunications and digital infrastructure market.
The IPO received approximately 1.39 crore applications, setting a new participation benchmark for India’s primary market.
Ahead of the public offering, Jio Platforms raised approximately ₹8,110 crore from 212 anchor investors.

Reliance Jio IPO: what’s behind the shift to a pure fundraise?
sum: Reliance Jio Platforms has reworked the structure of its planned Mumbai initial public offering, switching to a fully primary share sale after existing investors decided against selling stock amid market uncertainty linked to tensions in West Asia.
The revised plan means the offering will now be used solely to raise fresh capital for the company, according to two people familiar with the matter.

Provisions that would have allowed some shareholders to sell part of their holdings have been dropped, the people said, in a sign that current investors would rather stay exposed to the business than seek liquidity in a volatile market.
The change marks an important shift in how the listing is being framed.
A combined primary and secondary offering would have allowed the company to raise new money while also giving some early investors a route to cash out.
By moving to a fully primary structure, Jio is signalling that the float is now focused entirely on funding the company rather than creating an exit window for existing shareholders.
That distinction matters, especially at a time when sentiment is fragile.

items.t: Reliance shares tumble 4.6%, m-cap erodes ₹88,000 crore as windfall tax returns amid oil surge
sum: Shares of Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL), the country’s most valuable company by market capitalisation, came under severe selling pressure on Friday, 27 March, slipping 4.60% to the day’s low of ₹1,348 apiece and ending a two-day rally.

Friday's drop also marked the biggest single-day sell-off the stock has seen since June 2024, wiping out nearly ₹80,000 crore in market capitalisation. The sell-off in Mukesh Ambani-led company’s stock came after the government reintroduced windfall taxes on diesel and aviation turbine fuel (ATF) exports.

In a bid to ease pressure from rising crude oil prices—driven by the ongoing US–Israel–Iran conflict—the government on Friday cut excise duties on fuels, reducing petrol duty to ₹3 per litre and eliminating it on diesel. However, it also brought back the windfall tax, setting the diesel export tax at ₹21.5 per litre, along with a ₹29.5 per litre tax on aviation fuel exports.

India first imposed windfall profit taxes on 1 July 2022, joining a growing number of nations that tax supernormal profits of energy companies. At that time, export duties of ₹6 per litre each were levied on petrol and ATF, and ₹13 per litre on diesel, which was later scrapped on 2 December 2024, following a drop in crude oil prices.

The reintroduction of the windfall tax is likely to impact Reliance Industries, as it is the country’s largest fuel exporter. Its twin refineries at Jamnagar produce nearly 5 million tonnes of ATF, a significant portion of which is exported, accounting for about one-fourth of India's total ATF output, as per media reports.
In an exchange filing, the company also clarified that it has not purchased crude oil of Iranian origin, calling such claims “baseless” and misleading.

"Reliance Industries Limited categorically rejects recent media reports that the company has purchased crude oil of Iranian origin. These reports are baseless, leading to misleading and incorrect claims. We urge the concerned media outlets to verify facts before publication," the company said in its exchange filing on Thursday.

sum: The stock rebound comes as analysts highlighted that supply disruptions in the Middle East could lift refining margins, with diesel cracks already surging to $35-42 per barrel in recent days from around $20 per barrel earlier, leading to a potential windfall for the Mukesh Ambani-led conglomerate's oil-to-chemicals business.

"Every US$ 1/bbl higher refinery margin benefits Reliance's Ebitda by US$ 500mn annualized (2% of consol Ebitda for FY27)," Jefferies said in a note, adding that a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz could disrupt 2-3 million barrels per day of refined products, or 2-3% of global demand.

The brokerage said damage to Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery could lead to supply disruptions and higher refining margins, though it cautioned the benefit depends on whether the government reimposes windfall taxes on diesel and petrol.

JM Financial said the recent 8% decline in Reliance shares over the past month was excessive, arguing the company won't be negatively impacted by the spike in crude and liquefied natural gas prices. Instead, the firm expects near-term benefits from the jump in diesel cracks and a likely rise in petrochemical margins.

RIL's GRM could rise by USD 4-5/bbl. Every USD 1/bbl rise in RIL's GRM on an annualised basis results in an increase in its annual EBITDA by INR 45bn or 2.2% and increase in valuation by INR 29/share of 1.7%," JM Financial said, referring to gross refining margins.

"At CMP, RIL is trading near our bear-case valuation of ~INR 1,275/share," JM Financial said, maintaining its buy rating with an unchanged target price of Rs1,730. The firm attributed the recent correction largely to foreign institutional investor selling, with FII holdings declining to 21.1% at the end of December 2025 from a peak of 28.3% in March 2021.

The brokerage said current valuations adequately factor in near-term weakness in the retail business due to quick commerce competition but don't discount the 15-16% EBITDA growth story in the digital business over the next 2-3 years. At current levels, Reliance trades at 16.8 times fiscal 2028 estimated price-to-earnings, below its three-year average of 23.9 times, and 8.2 times fiscal 2028 estimated enterprise value-to-EBITDA versus a three-year average of 11.9 times.

sum: India has not received a single cargo of Venezuelan crude since May 2025 but Trump’s remarks have raised expectations of a resumption of trade. In 2024 Indian refiners imported an average of about 70,000 barrels per day from Venezuela with shipments exceeding 150,000 bpd in two months according to Kpler shipping data.

“Venezuelan crudes are heavy and sour and therefore cheaper and would be of interest to Indian refiners many of whom can process these types of crudes,” said Prashant Vasisht Senior Vice President and Co Group Head Corporate Ratings at ICRA Ltd. Reliance Industries’ refineries can process the extremely heavy and sour crude positioning the conglomerate as a direct beneficiary of any Venezuelan oil resumption.
Vasisht noted that for the Indian refining sector there are ample avenues including the US to purchase crude as Russian crude accounted for less than 2% of Indian crude imports prior to FY2023.

RIL shares have been under pressure amid uncertainty around Russian and Venezuela imports and are still down around 8% this calendar year so far. Its Q3 results which were also impacted by lower than expected performance in the retail business amid a slowdown in discretionary consumer spending offered investors little to chew on.

Reliance Industries Shares Drop Over 4% After Record High, Russian Oil Report Denial Weighs On Stock
sum: Mumbai: Shares of Reliance Industries Ltd. (RIL) fell sharply on Tuesday, January 6, a day after the stock touched its all-time high. The share price dropped over 4 percent to Rs 1,506.20 on the NSE, after hitting a record level of Rs 1,611.80 in the previous session. The fall surprised some investors as the stock had shown strong momentum just a day earlier.

The decline in Reliance shares came after the company strongly denied a media report claiming that Russian crude oil shipments were heading to its Jamnagar refinery. Reliance clarified that its refinery has not received any Russian oil cargo in the past three weeks and does not expect any such deliveries in January.

The company said it was “deeply pained” that its official denial was ignored before the report was published. The report had stated that three tankers carrying about 2.2 million barrels of Russian oil were signalling Jamnagar as their destination, based on data from analytics firm Kpler. Reliance called this claim completely untrue.

Despite the stock fall, global investment bank Jefferies remains positive on Reliance. In a note, Jefferies said Reliance and ONGC could benefit if the US takes control of Venezuelan oil production. Increased supply could reduce crude prices in 2027–28, unless OPEC+ steps in to control the market.

Jefferies added that if US sanctions on Venezuela are lifted, Reliance could again buy Venezuelan crude oil at cheaper rates. In the past, Reliance sourced around 20 percent of its daily crude needs from Venezuela at a discount of $5–8 per barrel to Brent crude, which helped improve its refining margins.

In late December 2025, RIL Chairman Mukesh Ambani shared a draft AI Manifesto. He said Reliance plans to become an AI-driven company and improve productivity ten times for its 6 lakh employees. Ambani called AI the most important technology of our time and said Reliance aims to provide affordable and safe AI for every Indian.

sum: Shares of oil marketing and refining companies, including Reliance Industries and Oil and Natural Gas Corporation (ONGC), traded with volatility in intraday deals on the BSE on Monday, January 5, following the US attack on Venezuela.

Reliance share price hit an all-time high of ₹1,611.20 but dropped over 1% from its peak to hit an intraday low of ₹1,588.70. On the other hand, ONGC's share price dropped over 2% to an intraday low of ₹235.75 after rising over 2% to an intraday high of ₹246.55.
The BSE Oil and Gas index declined by 1% during the session, a day after rising by almost 1%.

Reliance and ONGC shares, along with most other oil stocks, fell during Monday's session after a US military strike against Venezuela on Saturday, raising concerns that the geopolitical conflict could disrupt the oil market, as the Latin American country reportedly holds the largest known oil reserves.

While crude oil prices traded lower on Monday, there are concerns that a prolonged US-Venezuela conflict could escalate into a larger geopolitical crisis, potentially driving up crude oil prices and straining the margins of oil refiners.
Experts say that while tensions between the US and Venezuela have reintroduced a risk premium into global oil markets, their impact on Reliance Industries and ONGC may differ.
According to Seema Srivastava, Senior Research Analyst at SMC Global Securities, for ONGC, the impact is relatively straightforward.
